Prepay deals, membership details and a cost calculator

How a membership works

A small RFID tag on your windshield is your pass. Wash once a day, every day, for one monthly price.

  1. Sign up at the wash

    Pick Good, Better or Best. An attendant puts a small RFID tag on the inside of your windshield, and you can wash right away.

  2. Pull up to the entrance

    The scanner reads the tag as you roll in, so there's nothing to show or pay at the gate.

  3. Follow the attendant onto the track

    Someone from our team lines your front wheel up with the conveyor.

  4. Shift into neutral

    Hands off the wheel, foot off the brake. The conveyor pulls you through the whole wash.

  5. Drive off clean

    About two minutes later you're out the other end. Pull into a vacuum bay if you want to do the inside.

Same car, about two minutes apart

Drag the handle on any photo. Salt, spring mud and the grey film from a week of commuting all come off in one pass.

Road salt doesn't stop at the paint

From November to April, every trip down Hampton Road or out to Route 1 puts a fresh coat of salt and brine on your car. Most of it ends up underneath, where you can't see it and the rain won't rinse it off.

Left there, it works on brake lines, rocker panels, wheel wells and the exhaust. Better and Best include an undercarriage rinse with rust inhibitor, and with a membership, washing after every storm costs nothing extra.

  • Wash after every storm, not once in spring. Salt does its damage while it sits.
  • Choose a wash with an undercarriage rinse from the first snow until the street sweepers come out.
  • On a really cold day, open and close your doors once after the wash so the seals don't freeze shut.

How often to wash your car in a New Brunswick winter

Vacuums, under a roof

Free with any wash or membership, or $5 on their own. The six bays are covered, so you can do the floor mats in February without getting snowed on.

Easier on Kennebecasis Valley

A driveway wash can send 100 gallons of soapy, salty water down the storm drain. Our reclaim system treats and reuses nearly all of ours, for a net loss of about 10 to 12 gallons per vehicle.

All questions

How often can I wash with a membership?

Once a day, every day, at the level you signed up for. Members can also use the vacuums once a day, even on days they don't wash.

How long does a wash take?

Usually about two minutes through the tunnel. Right after a snowstorm there can be a short line, since everyone has the same idea.

Will my vehicle fit?

Most cars, SUVs and pickups fit. The clearance at the entrance is 7'2" (2.18 m), so if you have a roof box, a cargo or bike rack on top, or a very tall lifted truck, check your height first or ask the attendant. Very low or lowered cars can scrape getting onto the track, so if yours sits low, ask first.

Do I stay in my car?

Yes. Once the attendant has you lined up on the track, shift into neutral, take your hands off the wheel and keep your foot off the brake. Braking can knock the conveyor chain off its track, which shuts the wash down for everyone behind you.

How do I cancel or change my membership?

Come see us at the wash. Membership changes are made on site, not by phone or email. Cancelling needs at least 20 days' notice before your billing date, or you may be charged for one more month.

How can I pay?

We take all major credit cards, including Visa, Mastercard and American Express, plus Apple Pay and cash. Cash works for everything except a monthly membership, which bills automatically to a credit card.

Do the vacuums cost extra?

No, not with a wash. Vacuums are free with any wash and with every membership. If you only want to vacuum, it's $5.
